title: Does the optical pulse recover the heartbeat? PPG pulse rate vs ECG on BIDMC

dataset.name: BIDMC PPG and Respiration Dataset
dataset.record: 53 ICU recordings, simultaneous PLETH (PPG) + II (ECG) @ 125 Hz, 8 min each
dataset.citation: Pimentel MAF, Johnson AEW, Charlton PH, Birrenkott D, Watkinson PJ, Tarassenko L, Clifton DA. Toward a robust estimation of respiratory rate from pulse oximeters. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng. 2017;64(8):1914-23. Goldberger AL, et al. PhysioNet. Circulation. 2000;101(23):e215-20.

proposition: The PPG-derived pulse rate tracks the simultaneous ECG heart rate closely across 52 ICU recordings: Pearson r 0.96, Bland-Altman mean bias -2.1 bpm with 95% limits of agreement [-9.4, +5.1] bpm, mean absolute error 2.2 bpm, and 90% of records within +/-5 bpm of the ECG reference.

claims.statement: Pearson correlation of PPG pulse rate vs ECG heart rate across records
Bland-Altman lower 95% limit of agreement, bpm
Bland-Altman upper 95% limit of agreement, bpm
percent of records agreeing within +/-5 bpm

validation.reference: The simultaneous ECG heart rate (lead II R-peaks) as the gold-standard cardiac rate against which the PPG pulse rate is compared, per Bland-Altman method comparison
validation.data: REAL - BIDMC (PhysioNet), 53 ICU recordings with paired PLETH (PPG) + II (ECG)
validation.note: Aggregate acceptance: mean absolute error <= 5 bpm and >= 85% of records within +/-5 bpm (actual: MAE 2.2 bpm, 90.4% within 5 bpm, 96.2% within 10 bpm) - clearing the ANSI/AAMI EC13 heart-rate accuracy bar (+/-5 bpm / 10%). Honest scope: 1 of the 53 records (bidmc03) is excluded as an ECG-REFERENCE detection failure (the R-peak detector found only 225 beats -> an implausible 30 bpm, flagged objectively by ecg_hr < 40, not a PPG error); it is shown, not hidden. The largest surviving discrepancies (bidmc26, bidmc40) are records with poorer signal quality (ICU motion / arrhythmia), where agreement widens - reported in full.

open_questions.q: Agreement is a per-record mean pulse rate vs mean heart rate; beat-to-beat pulse-rate variability tracking (and its degradation under motion / arrhythmia / poor perfusion) is a finer question the paired signals support but this case does not pursue. Documented, not escalated.
